evidence.observation: A is shown head-on with a relatively deep, short body and a pale opercular area.
evidence.distinguishes_because: The current Y tile (I010 at 0.0) repeats this head-on shape and pale opercular mark, while X is side-on, supporting Y=A.

evidence.observation: B is shown side-on as a more elongated fish with dark shading near the caudal peduncle.
evidence.distinguishes_because: The current X tile (I007 at 0.0) shows the same side-on elongated profile and caudal shading, while Y is head-on, supporting X=B.

evidence.observation: X at the last time is a side-on fish with an elongated profile and the same caudal shading seen in B.
evidence.distinguishes_because: It matches the earlier B observation (I004) better than the earlier head-on A observation, making the X=B assignment more consistent.

decision.limitation: Fish are low-contrast and pose/orientation can change, so this identification relies mainly on overall body shape and spot/shading pattern rather than a single definitive landmark.
